newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks weak, electronics buck trend.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks weak, electronics buck trend.

text.p: Most Singapore shares ended weaker on Wednesday, but some electronic counters bucked the trend and fueled the electronic index to a new high.
The SES electronics index surged 3.39 points, or 2.54 percent, to end at 136.88 while the Straits Times Industrials fell 19.20 points, or 0.99 percent, to 1,917.89.
Multimedia Creative Technology, Electronic Resources, Flextech Holdings and Uraco were among the main stocks responsible for the surge in the electronic index.
"The electronic sector is benefitting from the good performance of U.S. high-tech stocks. Most of the Singapore companies are component suppliers to these U.S. firms," said one broker.
He said investors discounted Uraco's link with CAM International, which is affected by fraud allegations. Uraco bought a 6.48 percent stake in CAM last February.
"The focus is on its earnings potential. It supplies components to Nasdaq-listed Lam Research which is expected to post good growth over the next five years," he said.
At least one local brokerage revised upward its recommendation on Uraco to a "buy".
On Tuesday, Lam stocks jumped 17 percent after several U.S. houses raised it to a "buy" following an upbeat presentation at a trade show.
Uraco gained 9.09 percent to end at S$0.78 with more than 3.7 million shares traded. Creative hit a new high at S$32 before ending at S$31.90.

Breadmaker QAF Ltd was sold off amid confusion over its acquisition of instant noodle giant Indofood and concerns over the massive funding needed. Shares lost 10 cents to end at S$1.70 with over 4.9 million shares traded.
Car distributor and property firm Cycle & Carriage ended 60 cents lower at S$12.60 on concerns recent rise in Singapore's car quotas will squeeze its margins and profits.
Total market volume was around 149 million shares, with 162 gainers to 183 losers.
